title: Library-absent stubs and unreachable fallbacks
cluster_summary: The stub regime comes from library-stack.md (one setup file per adopted module, degrading to a stub) and testing-§8 (a parity case per adopted module). Packaging never strips LibKa0s, but under library-stack.md the major also goes absent when a module misses its floor or raises at load, for example on client API drift. So the stubs are reachable in rare runtime failures, not only on a hand-damaged install, and an open-evolutions question (U-3) will not retire them soon. U-3 is filed as an optional upstream design question and does not block anything. The cheap per-repo MUST breaches (AM-A-07, PM-A-03, LH-A-04, AT-A-07 Option A) are fixed now against the current standard rather than deferred. AT-A-16 is dead defensive code and is left alone.

verdicts.assessment: settings/Slash.lua:423 keeps a FormatRow stub with the em-dash join. slash-commands-§1 explicitly forbids that, and no deviation row covers it. The stub is reachable when the Slash major fails to load, the fix is about two lines, and U-3 is not a reason to leave a MUST breach in place.
verdicts.remediation: Red case first in the degraded suite: a degraded help or landing row contains neither '—' nor '|c'. Then drop the stub FormatRow member, build the row inline as '/am ' .. e[1] .. '  ' .. e[2], and fix the comment at :419-421.

verdicts.assessment: settings/Slash.lua:508-510 reproduces the coloured key = value format, and test_surface_parity.lua:193-194 byte-pins it against lib.FormatKV. That is the duplication slash-commands-§1 forbids, since only DISABLED_LINE_FORMAT may be carried. FormatKV must still exist on the degraded arm because the PANEL verbs call it. The fix is cheap.
verdicts.remediation: Keep Sl.FormatKV on the degraded arm but render it plainly as tostring(path) .. ' = ' .. tostring(valueStr). Replace the byte pin with a test that asserts the path and value are present and there is no '|c' escape, and rewrite the comment at :501-507. The stale testing.md:204 citation (PanelMaster/settings/Slash.lua:316) is a separate WowAddonStandards documentation fix; see PC-R-08.

verdicts.assessment: The facts hold: about 758 stub lines, enable-nolib-creation: no, and a stub mandated by library-stack.md. The premise is overstated, because a major is also absent when a module misses its floor or raises at load (client API drift), so the stubs are not reachable only on a hand-damaged install. There is no local defect. Whether the burden is worth it is a fair upstream design question, and it is not on the critical path.
verdicts.remediation: No PrettyChat change. Add an open-evolutions item (U-3) in WowAddonStandards, cross-referencing library-stack 'Ship payload vs adoption', slash-commands-§1 and testing-§8: given that a major goes absent through a load or floor failure rather than packaging, should an adopted major need a full member-answering stub plus a parity case, or only a one-line refusal at the entry points? In the same documentation pass, update the testing.md:204 worked example that still cites PanelMaster/settings/Slash.lua:316.

verdicts.assessment: DebugLogSetup always publishes NS.DebugLog (stub or live) with Toggle and RunDiagnostics, so the 'Debug console unavailable' arms in settings/Slash.lua are dead. They are harmless defensive code, and the auditor already marked them not filed.

core/PerfSetup.lua builds a Perf stub, but test_surface_parity.lua has no Perf case. testing-§8 is a MUST, and test_slash_degraded.lua only touches a few members. The fix is one cheap case, and the stub is reachable on a load failure of Perf, which floors on both Core and Lifecycle.
verdicts.remediation: Add a Perf case to tests/test_surface_parity.lua with its '-- members from: grep' comment covering on, suspended, BUCKET_ORDER, Note, Open, Close, Suspend, Resume and OnCommand, asserted on the live arm and on the degraded arm from tests/degraded_env.lua.

verdicts.assessment: modules/Bar.lua:15 and modules/Display.lua:26-27 resolve LibKa0s-Widgets-1.0 inline, with no setup file, stub, parity case or register row, against library-stack.md and testing-§8. The degraded behaviour is honest. The #26 part is out of date: #26 is closed will-not-do, and its 2026-09-23 AT-DOCS comment already limits the decline to Dropdown and records DragHandle as adopted, so no #26 note is needed.
verdicts.remediation: Option A: add core/WidgetsSetup.lua that resolves LibStub('LibKa0s-Widgets-1.0', true) and publishes NS.Widgets with a nil-answering DragHandle stub and DRAG_HANDLE, add an annotated TOC line before the modules, switch Bar.lua and Display.lua to NS.Widgets, and add a grep-derived Widgets parity case on both arms in tests/test_surface_parity.lua. Update docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:49-51. Do not comment on #26.
